messages:
customer_jules: Hey team — hitting a bad case where streaming responses cut off mid-json and then we get charged for duplicated tokens after a reconnect. Happening on both our Node frontend (TS SDK) and Python backend. Started after last SDK patch.

nina: Sorry you're seeing that. Can you paste a minimal repro and timestamps? Which model / region?

customer_jules: Model: redwood/opt-3.2. Region: us-west-2. First seen 2025-11-24T18:12:03Z. Quick repro: open stream, abort connection client-side, reconnect immediately. Often final chunk never arrives, then subsequent reconnect produces overlapping tokens in logs.

eng-matt: @nina can you capture the raw SSE frames and any edge logs? This sounds like resume-handshake + heartbeat timing issue.

customer_jules: Attached logs snippet:

```
> SSE chunk: {"id":1,"tokens":[...],"final":true}
> client abort -> reconnect
> SSE chunk: {"id":1,"tokens":[...],"final":true}  // duplicate
> billing: charged for both
```

alex.s: Thanks. Two separate failure modes I've seen: 1) client-side duplicate resume token replay (SDK re-sends last seq on fast reconnect) and 2) proxy handoff where edge buffers final frame and then forward during new connection causing duplicate final frame. Need to confirm which is happening here.

nina: Can you run with debug headers: `X-RW-Trace: jules-case`, `X-Heartbeat-Interval: 1500` and share raw frames? Also include SDK versions.

customer_jules: TS SDK 3.4.1, Python SDK 2.9.0. Logs with headers: attached.

support-bot: Incident created INC-2025-789 (assigned to eng-matt) :rotating_light:

eng-matt: I dug into the traces. I see interleaved timestamps where edge proxy (internal edge-02) ACKs final frame ~120ms after client closed socket, and then resume handshake from new connection replays the server-side cached final chunk. That matches the buffered-handoff hypothesis. The SDK repro shows the TS client sends resume with same resume_id immediately after abort; our server currently treats resume as "replay allowed" for a short window and returns cached fragments which can duplicate billing.

alex.s: Repro steps I ran locally: 1) start generator, 2) stream until partial, 3) call `controller.abort()` in 10ms window, 4) open new EventSource with same session id. Observed duplicated final JSON about 30% of runs. Patch in TS SDK that started shipping recently changed premature close behavior and made it more likely to reuse seq id on restart.

nina: Short-term mitigation options: - advise customer to add jitter to reconnection or increase client heartbeat interval to 2s. - disable automatic resume in TS SDK (flag) until we issue server-side dedupe.

eng-matt: Long-term: server will dedupe final-frame delivery by checking (resume_id, seq) pairs and refusing to deliver cached fragments already acknowledged to a different socket. Also we should make billing idempotent for resumed frames within a 30s window. I'll open runtime PR.

alex.s: Also sending a small SDK patch to avoid resending the last seq when reconnect happens within 100ms; that should reduce the race. I'll open PR referencing INC-2025-789.

customer_jules: Appreciate fast triage. Is there an ETA for the server-side fix? Currently this is hitting our billing and truncation fallback logic.

nina: Eng-matt estimates 3 days for a staged rollout (canary edge + server change) if no regressions. Workaround: set `resume: false` in TS SDK config OR increase reconnect delay >200ms.

eng-matt: For debugging, please include a pcap of a repro run and the raw EventSource frames (no pretty print). I'll attach a small script you can run to generate deterministic repro.

customer_jules: Will run and post pcap. Thanks.

eng-matt: Follow-up actions: 1) alex.s to open SDK PR to make resume opt-in + add jitter (in flight). 2) eng-matt to open runtime PR for dedupe + billing idempotency (INC-2025-789). 3) Support to notify customer with workaround and ETA (nina).

nina: Noted. Updating ticket and scheduling a sync with the customer tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
